findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A pytest repo configures an always-test entry and uses `pytest` or `pytest tests` as its test command.
Appending the entry as a positional argument makes pytest collect only that entry when the command otherwise relies on `testpaths`. With pytest 8, an entry under an explicitly named directory can also suppress other files in that directory. The run can therefore pass while skipping changed tests or the shared-input full fallback. See the [pytest collection issue](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13494).
findings.title: Functional: Preserve selected pytest files when always-test entries are present

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - An existing mixed Python and JavaScript repo has `fast_test = "forge test --pytest {base}"` and a full test command containing pytest and Vitest or Jest.
The picker now removes the JavaScript runner, installation, and Node checks. `review.close_test` uses an existing `fast_test` unchanged, so close can pass without running any JavaScript tests even when they fail. The new mixed-repo suggestion adds separate Node steps, but it does not repair existing settings.
findings.title: Functional: Keep JavaScript checks in existing mixed-repo fast tests

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A repo runs separate unit and integration Vitest or Jest commands, or its npm test script also runs a type check.
The repeated-kind check drops the second runner, so the suggested `fast_test` can pass without running integration tests. Separately, `test_parts` classifies a compound npm script by any runner in its body, and line 87 appends runner flags to the whole script; for `vitest run && tsc --noEmit`, those flags reach `tsc` and make the suggested command fail.
findings.title: Functional: Preserve JavaScript test commands in quick-test advice

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A Python repo has `pyproject.toml` and runs `python -m unittest discover`.
The Python manifest alone causes doctor and upgrade to suggest `forge test --pytest`, although the configured command does not invoke pytest. When one test file is related and another is excluded, `narrow_command` appends `-p _forge_pytest_selection`; unittest treats `-p` as its [file-discovery pattern](https://docs.python.org/3/library/unittest.html#test-discovery), runs zero matching tests, and can return success.
findings.title: Functional: Do not suggest the pytest picker for other Python runners

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A repo configures `test = "cd web && npx vitest run"` and relies on `forge test --change` or close.
Each part now runs in a separate shell. The `cd` succeeds in one process, but Vitest starts from the repository root in another, so it can run the wrong project's tests or fail to find the web project.
findings.title: Functional: Preserve the shell directory for JavaScript test steps

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A developer runs `forge test --pytest origin/main` from a source or test subdirectory.
The command now reads `forge.toml` from the current directory rather than resolving and entering the checkout root. It raises a file-not-found error instead of running the selected tests; the CLI does not change directories before invoking this handler.
